scope: Read-only re-scoring and comparison of frozen controlled baseline traces; no candidate implementation, new game, seed, rollout or experiment.

conclusions.legal_support: All missed moves are in the exact public prestate legal action set. No legality exclusion caused any of these misses.
conclusions.hypothesis_support: The two-point behavioral distribution excludes the actual contest move in all ten misses. This is missing behavioral hypothesis support, not missing game-rule legality.
conclusions.weights: All ten missed states have identical complete joint actions in both hypotheses and neither includes the contested destination. Any normalized nonnegative reweighting of those same two hypotheses keeps probability zero. The six covered contests have one supporting hypothesis and probability 0.5; their calibration is separate.
conclusions.public_state: Saved public-state digests, stored hypotheses, actual revealed choices, selected execution first-step prestate/hypotheses, and legal actions reproduce exactly. The actual controller also reproduces from each saved prestate. No observed state/chronology mismatch found.
conclusions.behavioral_difference: All ten misses occur under goal both with the rival unsecured: enemy_hypotheses takes routes(...)[0], which is eliminate while enemy elimination is incomplete; reference explicitly prioritizes secure until that team secures. All missed contesters already have firing access, so their eliminate-distance gain for the central move is zero and shooting wins the tactical score. The actual secure objective favors entering the zone.
conclusions.coordination: No missed central move is removed by within-enemy reservation: each missed contester is the first living enemy actor, and the contested move has tactical score zero versus a positive shoot score. Actual reference decisions are independent and may collide with their own allies (e.g. ego592 tick7 enemies4/5 both target8:2).
conclusions.chronology: validation_experiment.combat commits focal choices, calls opponent(w, actor, seed, rival) on unchanged w, then resolve(w, choices,...). opponent receives no pending choices. First-step forecast likewise computes theirs from unchanged model=w, not from first/ours. Both can respond to prior resolved public positions/HP/ammo, but neither can react to the focal current candidate/root. Later forecast depths legitimately depend on previously simulated joint actions.
conclusions.reference_preview: The actual reference comparator evaluates single-action previews with other players stationary. Each missed central move has secure progress 0.4375 -> 0.6666666667 in that uncontested preview, including first capture hold. In the actual joint resolution the matching focal move causes collision. This stationary preview is a documented controller-model assumption, not a stale or different observed prestate.

metric_definition: A contest is a focal chosen move destination also proposed by at least one living enemy on the same tick. This is competing simultaneous intent, not existing occupancy: legal() already excludes pre-occupied cells. Counts are per focal move; these 16 observations happen to each have exactly one focal and one enemy contester.
